**Research Question:**
How have malaria incidence trends and inequalities evolved across SADC countries from 2000–2024?

## Setup

```{r setup, include=FALSE}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)

```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(nlme)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(modelsummary)

```


# Loading the data

```{r}

malaria_inc <- read_csv("/Users/careenevansjoseph/Downloads/incidence-of-malaria/Malaria incidence.csv",show_col_types = FALSE)

glimpse(malaria_inc)

```


```{r}

malaria_full <- malaria_inc %>%
  setNames(c("country", "code", "year", "incidence"))

glimpse(malaria_full)

```


# Data inspection

## Study period

```{r}

range(malaria_full$year,na.rm = TRUE)

```

## Number of countries

```{r}

malaria_full %>% summarise(n_countries = n_distinct(country))

```

## Country coverage

```{r}

country_coverage <- malaria_full %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    first_year = min(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_year = max(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_years = n_distinct(year),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(country)

country_coverage

```

## Missing values

```{r}

malaria_full %>%
  summarise(
    missing_country = sum(is.na(country)),
    missing_code = sum(is.na(code)),
    missing_year = sum(is.na(year)),
    missing_incidence = sum(is.na(incidence))
  )

```


```{r}

malaria_full %>%
  count(country, year) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

```


# Defining SADC countries

```{r}

SADC_countries <- c(
  "Angola", "Botswana", "Comoros", 
  "Democratic Republic of the Congo",
  "Eswatini", "Lesotho", "Madagascar", "Malawi", "Mauritius", 
  "Mozambique", "Namibia", "Seychelles", "South Africa", 
  "Tanzania", "Zambia", "Zimbabwe"
)

```

Check which SADC countries are missing from the dataset:

```{r}

setdiff(
  SADC_countries,
  unique(malaria_full$country)
)

```



```{r}

malaria_sadc_data <- malaria_full %>%
  filter(country %in% SADC_countries)

```



```{r}

malaria_sadc_data %>%
  summarise(
    n_countries = n_distinct(country),
    n_observations = n()
  )

```


# SADC country coverage

```{r}

SADC_coverage <- malaria_sadc_data %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    first_year = min(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_year = max(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_years = n_distinct(year),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(country)

SADC_coverage

```

```{r}

malaria_sadc_data %>%
  count(country)

```


# Missing values

```{r}

malaria_sadc_data %>%
  summarise(
    total = n(),
    missing_incidence = sum(is.na(incidence)),
    missing_year = sum(is.na(year))
  )

```


# Descriptive statistics

```{r}

SADC_descriptive <- malaria_sadc_data %>%
```

# Distribution of malaria incidence

## Histogram

```{r}

ggplot(
  malaria_sadc_data,
  aes(x = incidence)
) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of malaria incidence",
    x = "Malaria incidence per 1,000 population at risk",
    y = "Number of observations"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

## Log-scale histogram

Because incidence differs between countries

```{r}

ggplot(malaria_sadc_data,
  aes(x = incidence)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of malaria incidence on a log scale",
    x = "Malaria incidence per 1,000 population at risk (log scale)",
    y = "Number of observations") +
  theme_minimal()

```


# Distribution by country

```{r}

ggplot(malaria_sadc_data,
  aes(x = incidence)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ country, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of malaria incidence by country",
    x = "Country",
    y = "Malaria incidence per 1,000 population at risk"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```


# log incidence

```{r}

summary(malaria_sadc_data$incidence)

```


```{r}

sum(malaria_sadc_data$incidence <= 0, na.rm = TRUE)

```

```{r}

malaria_sadc_data <- malaria_sadc_data %>%
  mutate(
    log_incidence = log(incidence)
  )

```

The log transformation allows to model **relative changes in incidence** and reduces the influence of very high-incidence observations.

# Country-specific trends


```{r}

country_trends <- malaria_sadc_data %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  do(
    tidy(
      lm(incidence ~ year, data = .),
      conf.int = TRUE
    )
  )

```
 
year coefficients:

```{r}

country_trends_year <- country_trends %>%
  filter(term == "year") %>%
  select(
    country,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value,
    conf.low,
    conf.high
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, conf.low, conf.high),
      ~ round(.x, 2)
    )
  )

country_trends_year

```

# Change between 2000 and 2024

```{r}

SADC_change <- malaria_sadc_data %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2000, 2024)) %>%
  select(country, year, incidence) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year,
    names_prefix = "Y",
    values_from = incidence
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    incidence_ratio = Y2024 / Y2000,
    log_incidence_ratio = log(Y2024 / Y2000),
    percent_change = ((Y2024 - Y2000) / Y2000) * 100
  )

#  results
SADC_change
```

# Longitudinal mixed-effects model

Now we move to the **main longitudinal analysis**.

First, a random-intercept model:

```{r}

mixed_model_1 <- lmer(log_incidence ~ year + (1 | country),data = malaria_sadc_data,REML = TRUE)


```

### Interpretation

This model estimates the overall temporal trend while allowing countries to have different baseline incidence levels.


# Allow countries to have different trends

```{r}

mixed_model_2 <- lmer(log_incidence ~ year + (year | country), data = malaria_sadc_data,REML = TRUE)

```

```{r}
modelsummary(
  list(
    "Random Intercept" = mixed_model_1,
    "Random Slope & Intercept" = mixed_model_2
  ),
  stars = TRUE,
  statistic = "conf.int",
  gof_omit = "IC|Log|F",
  title = "Table 1: Mixed-Effects Models for Malaria Log-Incidence"
)
```


#  Comparing the mixed models

```{r}

anova(
  mixed_model_1,
  mixed_model_2
)

```

# changing the overall time coefficient to annual percentage change

Extract the year coefficient:

```{r}

year_coefficient <- fixef(mixed_model_2)["year"]

year_coefficient

```

Converting it to an approximate annual percentage change:

```{r}

annual_percent_change <- (exp(year_coefficient) - 1) * 100

annual_percent_change

```


```{r}

round(annual_percent_change, 2)

```


# Model assumptions

## Residual vs fitted values

```{r}
plot(mixed_model_2, resid(., type = "pearson") ~ fitted(.), abline = 0)
```

## Normal Q-Q plot

```{r}

qqnorm(resid(mixed_model_2))

qqline(resid(mixed_model_2))

```

## Residual distribution

```{r}

ggplot(data.frame(residuals = resid(mixed_model_2)),
  aes(x = residuals)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of model residuals",
    x = "Residuals",
    y = "Number of observations") +
  theme_minimal()

```

# Temporal autocorrelation

```{r}

residual_data <- malaria_sadc_data %>%
  mutate(residual = residuals(mixed_model_2),
    fitted = fitted(mixed_model_2))

ggplot(
  residual_data,
  aes(x = year,y = residual)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0,linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ country) +
  labs(title = "Residuals over time by country",x = "Year",y = "Model residual") +
  theme_minimal()

```

# Model with AR(1) temporal correlation

Because measurements close together in time within a country may be correlated, we can explicitly model this using an AR(1) correlation structure.

```{r}

ar1_model <- gls(log_incidence ~ year + country, correlation = corAR1(form = ~ year | country),
  data = malaria_sadc_data, method = "REML")

```

This model accounts for the fact that:

> incidence in a country in one year may be correlated with incidence in the previous year. Relevant for a 2000–2024 country panel.


# Country-specific trends with temporal correlation

 Qn:
> Do malaria incidence trends differ between SADC countries?


```{r}

ar1_interaction_model <- gls(log_incidence ~ year * country, correlation = corAR1(form = ~ year | country),
  data = malaria_sadc_data, method = "REML")

```

```{r}
modelsummary(
  list(
    "AR(1) Main Effects" = ar1_model,
    "AR(1) Interaction" = ar1_interaction_model
  ),
  stars = TRUE,
  gof_omit = "IC|Log|F",
  title = "Table 2: Generalized Least Squares Models with AR(1) Autocorrelation"
)
```



# Comparing models

```{r}
anova(ar1_model, ar1_interaction_model)
```



# country-specific annual trends
```{r}
library(emmeans)
```


```{r}
country_slopes <- emtrends(ar1_interaction_model, ~ country, var = "year")

country_slopes

```

Confidence interval

```{r}

country_slopes_ci <- summary(country_slopes, infer = TRUE)
country_slopes_ci
```

Converting the log slopes to annual percentage changes

```{r}
country_APC <- country_slopes_ci %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    annual_percent_change =
      (exp(year.trend) - 1) * 100
  ) %>%
  select(country,year.trend,SE,lower.CL,upper.CL,annual_percent_change)

country_APC

```


```{r}

country_APC %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric),
      ~ round(.x, 2)
    )
  )

```


# Inequality between SADC countries

```{r}

annual_inequality <- malaria_sadc_data %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_incidence = mean(incidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_incidence = median(incidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_incidence = sd(incidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25 = quantile(incidence, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75 = quantile(incidence, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_incidence = min(incidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_incidence = max(incidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

annual_inequality

```


# Plotting the annual range of incidence

```{r}

ggplot(
  annual_inequality,
  aes(x = year)
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = q25,
      ymax = q75
    ),
    alpha = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = median_incidence),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of malaria incidence across SADC countries over time",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Malaria incidence per 1,000 population at risk",
    caption = "Line shows the annual median; shaded area shows the interquartile range."
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```


#  Inequality on the log scale

```{r}

annual_log_inequality <- malaria_sadc_data %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_log_incidence = mean(log_incidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_log_incidence = median(log_incidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_log_incidence = sd(log_incidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25 = quantile(log_incidence, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75 = quantile(log_incidence, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

```


```{r}

ggplot(
  annual_log_inequality,
  aes(x = year)
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = q25,
      ymax = q75
    ),
    alpha = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = median_log_incidence),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Relative distribution of malaria incidence across SADC countries",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Log malaria incidence"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```


# Check whether the relationship with time is linear


```{r}

ggplot(
  malaria_sadc_data,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = log_incidence
  )
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess",
    se = TRUE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Overall temporal pattern of malaria incidence",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Log malaria incidence"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```


# Nonlinear sensitivity analysis


```{r}

nonlinear_model <- gls(
  log_incidence ~ year + I(year^2) + country,
  correlation = corAR1(
    form = ~ year | country
  ),
  data = malaria_sadc_data,
  method = "REML"
)

summary(nonlinear_model)

```


```{r}
anova(
  ar1_model,
  nonlinear_model
)

```

```{r}
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = q25,
      ymax = q75
    ),
    alpha = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = median_incidence),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of malaria incidence across SADC countries over time",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Malaria incidence per 1,000 population at risk",
    caption = "Line shows the annual median; shaded area shows the interquartile range."
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  "03_output/figures/inequality.png",
  plot = p,
  width = 10,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300
)


# Inequality on log scale
p <- ggplot(
  annual_log_inequality,
  aes(x = year)
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = q25,
      ymax = q75
    ),
    alpha = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = median_log_incidence),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Relative distribution of malaria incidence across SADC countries",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Log malaria incidence"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  "03_output/figures/log_inequality.png",
  plot = p,
  width = 10,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300
)


# LOESS temporal pattern
p <- ggplot(
  malaria_sadc_data,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = log_incidence
  )
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess",
    se = TRUE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Overall temporal pattern of malaria incidence",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Log malaria incidence"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  "03_output/figures/temporal_pattern_loess.png",
  plot = p,
  width = 10,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300
)


# Residuals vs fitted values
png(
  "03_output/figures/residuals_vs_fitted.png",
  width = 2000,
  height = 1600,
  res = 300
)

plot(
  mixed_model_2,
  resid(., type = "pearson") ~ fitted(.),
  abline = 0
)

dev.off()


# Normal Q-Q plot
png(
  "03_output/figures/normal_qq_plot.png",
  width = 2000,
  height = 1600,
  res = 300
)

qqnorm(resid(mixed_model_2))
qqline(resid(mixed_model_2))

dev.off()
```
